title: Invocation mismatch hypotheses journal
content:
Context:
I've been chasing a sporadic failure where function/tool-invocations from the hosted API sometimes arrive at downstream services with the wrong shape or as an already-stringified blob. This started after the August rollout of the streaming gateway change; frequency seems correlated with high-concurrency bursts (p95 token latency spikes).

High-level symptom summary (user-facing):
- App calls Redwood API with function_call:{name: "extract_entities", arguments: {...}}
- API response occasionally contains 'arguments' as a string (escaped JSON) or a truncated partial JSON snippet, causing the consumer to fail JSON.parse() or to validate against schema and reject.
- When the function call is returned via streaming mode to client, the client sometimes receives an early function name without corresponding full arguments.

Examples captured from debug traces:
1) Raw response fragment (from debug wiretap):
{
  "name": "extract_entities",
  "arguments": "{\"text\":\"Order 1823: 2x coffee\",\"meta\":{...}"
}
-- note: arguments is a JSON string, double-escaped in transport

2) Truncated streaming output (client-side reassembled chunks):
[chunk1] {"name": "extract_entities", "arguments": {"text": "Ship to 12 Main St"
[chunk2] , "meta": {"id": 84} }
-- chunk boundaries sometimes split in the middle of braces; reassembly logic fails when client assumes single-chunk function payloads

3) Internal service log (downstream parsing error):
2025-10-29T15:22:11Z ERR parse_failed service=entity-extractor err="Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 1" request_id=rx-1a2b

Commands/experiments I've run so far (notes + outputs):
- Reproduced locally with rdw-cli: rdw invoke --model redwood-3b --stream true --fn extract_entities --input samples/order-1823.json
  -> Observed same double-escaped arguments when enabling --stream and using small chunk-size (rdw runtime set to chunk-size=128).
- rdw-cli with --stream false => arguments object preserved as JSON, no escapes.
- Grepped runtime logs for streaming encoder errors: grep -n "stream.*escape" /var/log/rdw/*.log -> no consistent error strings, but timestamps align with latency spikes.
- Enabled TRACE for stream-assembler and io-layer: found intermittent call to assembler.serialize_as_string(true) inside a fallback path when chunk reassembly buffer exceeded threshold.
- Added unit test in stream-assembler that simulates chunk cuts across UTF-8 multibyte characters -> passed initially, but when combined with prefix-caching enabled it failed to reassemble braces correctly.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Reassembly fallback coerces argument objects to strings when buffer/latency constraints hit, to avoid blocking high-priority streams. (High plausibility; we found assembler.serialize_as_string(true) in trace.)
2) Double-escaping happens at two layers: streaming encoder frames JSON text and the downstream serializer also quotes fields when encountering streaming-phase markers. Race condition between encoder and serializer causes one to treat an object as "opaque" and JSON.stringify it. (Medium plausibility.)
3) Tokenization/byte-splitting across UTF-8 multibyte characters causes the reassembler to miscalculate brace boundaries; as a defensive measure some codepath wraps the partial payload to keep it valid JSON by quoting it. (Lower plausibility but explains correlation with chunk-size and certain inputs.)
4) Client-side reassembly logic assumes a framing pattern that changed in the gateway rollout; clients that didn't update assume single-frame function args and therefore mis-handle chunked messages rather than the server sending strings. (Possible, but I can reproduce server-side with rdw-cli)

Quick notes from code inspection:
- stream/assembler.go: on buffer overflow -> fallbackSerializeAsString() which returns JSON string of buffer. This is by design for previous use-case (log-safe truncation) but not correct for function-call payloads.
- io/encoder.py: has a flag quote_on_stream_boundary default false; but router sets it true under high concurrency. Need to trace who flips it.
- prefix_cache decorator (in runtime service) can short-circuit reassembly by returning cached prefix as already-serialized bytes. If cache contains a stringified form for a previous call, new reassembly path may reuse it incorrectly.

Immediate mitigation(s) attempted in staging:
- Disable fallbackSerializeAsString for function-call paths by adding early return when content_type=="fncall" -> staging shows reduced occurrences in a 2-hour smoke test.
- Increase stream assembler buffer limits from 8k -> 32k in staging; reduced overflow rate but not eliminated under synthetic concurrency test (1000 rps burst).
- Add additional validation at gateway: if function payload is detected as string, attempt JSON.parse and if success, re-inject parsed object into payload (temporary band-aid). This masked some customer errors but felt fragile.

Metrics to gather next (instrumentation):
- Count of stream assembler fallback events per minute tagged by route/model/function_type
- Histogram of chunk sizes and frequency of UTF-8 split bytes near chunk boundaries
- Correlate fallback events with prefix-cache hits/misses
- Trace-level sampling for requests that hit fallback path (capture full chunk sequence)

Repro steps for a minimal test-case (notes for QA):
1) Use rdw-cli (local) with runtime configuration: streaming enabled, chunk-size=128, prefix-cache enabled, prefix-cache-ttl=60s
2) invoke model with a function_call where arguments contain multibyte characters and nested objects (payload attached in samples/test-fn-multibyte.json)
3) Observe rdw-cli reassembled output and the wiretap in staging (or simulated wiretap) for double-escaped arguments or truncated JSON

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Remove fallbackSerializeAsString for structured payloads (function calls, tool outputs) and implement a safe truncation that preserves JSON structure (replace interior with "...TRUNCATED..." placeholder while keeping outer braces).
- Make stream assembler aware of message schema: if content_type==fncall, enforce object-mode reassembly and reject the fallback-stringify path.
- Ensure prefix_cache stores canonical parsed representation, not a serialized string; treat cached entries as typed objects with reserialization done as final step.
- Add end-to-end integration tests for streaming function call paths with a variety of chunk sizes and unicode payloads.

Open questions / unknowns to investigate:
- Who toggles io/encoder.quote_on_stream_boundary under high load? Need to trace router policy changes during rollout (possible config flag that was enabled globally).
- Does the gateway streaming framing spec changed subtly in Aug rollout? Compare commit diffs and changelog for gateway.
- Is there any intermediary (edge CDN, proxy) that rewrites bodies and may coerce content? So far negative.

Immediate next actions (assigned):
- Diego: add metric for assembler.fallback_count and tag by content_type (done: PR opened GH:runtime#873).
- Lina: instrument prefix_cache to log when cached entry type is "stringified" vs "object" for lookups (in progress).
- Me (Asha): prepare a small patch to disable fallbackSerializeAsString for content_type==fncall and run 24h smoke test in staging; collect failing traces post-patch.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep customer-facing incident wording non-technical: "intermittent function argument serialization issue under high-concurrency streaming; mitigation applied; full fix planned"
- Add a short snippet to docs/clients about robust client reassembly (defensive parse attempts) until server-side fix is rolled out; make sure not to encourage tolerating escaped args as permanent pattern.

Attachments / snippets to drop into ticket (paste-ready):
- wiretap fragment: {"name": "extract_entities", "arguments": "{\"text\":\"Order 1823\"}"}
- stack trace summary: assembler.serialize_as_string -> stream/assembler.go:412 -> router/stream_handler.py:127 -> gateway/main.py:89

Priority: P1 for customers hitting failures in production; P2 for overall error class.

End of notes.

(If I come back in a week: check whether default chunk-size was reverted in prod; and whether rollout flag for streaming framing was toggled during same release window.)
